target_customer: Independent and community pharmacies in the UK that want to offer diagnostic and blood testing services
problem: Patients wait or travel far for diagnostic tests while independent pharmacies lack the clinical, lab and software setup to offer them.
business_model: B2B2C software and service: pharmacies sell and fulfil tests through Tuli, with lab partners; revenue share on tests and phlebotomy network fees

founders.name: Jiawei Li
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him with no background. A conference speaker snippet describes a medical background (UCL medicine), not confirmed on a page I opened.

founders.name: Jialu Tu
founders.background_notes: YC page: close to 10 years in financial services before moving to healthcare startups; employers not named.

competitors.name: Medicspot
competitors.what: Supplied COVID PCR tests and a compliance support tool to pharmacies, partnered with the National Pharmacy Association
competitors.traction_then: NPA members offered 16 to 28 percent discounts on PCR kits

competitors.name: NHS Pharmacy Collect (free lateral flow tests)
competitors.what: Free rapid tests handed out through pharmacies, which undercut paid testing for some customers
competitors.traction_then: Rolled out to more than nine in ten pharmacies by April 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking, ordering and results software plus lab logistics; the hard parts were clinical governance and lab partnerships rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: CQC registration and a network of pharmacy partners help, but other test suppliers sold to the same pharmacies and the COVID test revenue was temporary.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large chains and suppliers sold testing in 2021. No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Tuli.

market_need_then: UK demand for private COVID PCR and lateral flow testing in 2021 and about 11,000 independent pharmacies without a turnkey testing setup, per the YC page.

identity.logo: A T logo mark per a directory listing; no design details sourced
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain healthcare access language such as key services available from every high street

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; the name is easily confused with Tula Health and Tulea Health in search results.

pivots.from: Selling and fulfilling COVID-19 tests through pharmacies
pivots.to: Blood testing and phlebotomy network through community pharmacies
pivots.why: COVID test demand fell; the current site shows blood testing, phlebotomy and enterprise services; exact date not found

outcome_analysis: Tuli launched in June 2021 selling COVID tests through 147 pharmacies and claimed over 7,000 tests, then moved to a blood testing and phlebotomy network that its site says reaches 308 pharmacy partners and is CQC registered. The company is still Active with roughly ten staff per directories. Funding is not verifiable beyond YC, so it appears capital efficient or small, and the pivot away from COVID testing is the main reason it survived.
notes: Funding unverified: Village.ai and Seedtable show 125k from Y Combinator and Asymmetry Ventures; Welcome to the Jungle shows two seed rounds in August and December 2021 totalling about 0.3M; Persana says undisclosed. Each is a single aggregator, so no rounds are recorded. Somacap lists a 2017 founding, likely wrong. The pivot date is unknown. Completeness pass: rounds are recorded but each rests on a single database (Seedtable/Extruct for 125K dated 2021-09; Welcome to the Jungle for seed rounds in 2021-08 and 2021-12, amounts not split, about 0.3M total). These sources conflict and may overlap, so amounts are not summed.
